en.askTitle: Change the boxes to your own income and savings and test a Lisbon-area home price before you talk to a bank
en.runTitle: Lisbon: a Brazilian couple with EUR 70,000 saved and a first two-bedroom flat in mind

fields.label: Ages and residence or permit details
fields.value: a Brazilian couple in our early 30s, living in Lisbon since 2024 on residence permits

fields.label: Tax residence and ownership history, including Brazilian or inherited rights
fields.placeholder: e.g. tax-resident in Portugal since 2024; one of us co-owns an inherited flat in Brazil

fields.label: Gross and net salary plus payment frequency
fields.value: EUR 3,600 gross a month as a software engineer at a Portuguese company

fields.label: Freelance accounts and net income
fields.value: freelancing on recibos verdes at EUR 2,000 a month

fields.label: Commute needs
fields.placeholder: e.g. one of us goes to central Lisbon four days a week

en.template: Help us plan a first T2 permanent-home purchase near Lisbon for {move}. We are {profile}, with {taxhistory}, {salary}, {freelance}, {savings} and {commute}. Compare Almada and Amadora first. Test the price against accepted net income, actual LTV, appraisal, acquisition-date tax relief, closing costs and a positive stressed household budget. Keep {reserve} untouched. Separate dated listing examples from verified availability, list the personal facts still needed, and ask before contacting anyone, sharing documents or submitting an application.

phases.title: Read the bank regulator, tax office and lender pages that decide what they can borrow and pay
phases.note: Mortgage limits, purchase taxes, young-buyer relief and closing costs
phases.judgment: Where two Banco de Portugal pages disagreed (50% versus 45% of net income going to debt payments), the researcher flagged the conflict and used the dedicated current page’s 45%, while marking the stress-test method as unverified.

phases.title: Collect dated two-bedroom examples in six areas and build the affordability guide
phases.note: Price per square metre, monthly payments and the price they can actually afford
phases.judgment: The price researcher withdrew earlier draft claims it could not re-open and kept twelve listing examples (seven from full listing pages, five labelled as listing cards), all marked as examples and not as available homes.

phases.title: Independent check of every figure, then desktop and phone layout tests
phases.judgment: The reviewer recomputed everything (146 of 146 checks passed) and still pushed back on three wordings. One example: at EUR 300,000 with EUR 3,500 net a month, the stressed budget leaves only EUR 0.06 a month.

workers: Checked Banco de Portugal’s mortgage limits and the public rate and fee pages of several banks
Worked out the purchase taxes, young-buyer relief and closing costs from the tax office’s own pages, with examples at five prices
Collected twelve asking-price examples for two-bedroom flats across six areas, plus the national statistics office’s price data
Recomputed every money figure independently and checked the guide’s claims against its sources
